titulo: Delivery with agents: one folder per client, human gates and secrets kept out
lead: Agents do the repetitive work: run the X-ray, build the report, suggest titles, write the draft. What gives the client confidence is that nothing goes live without a human approving it, and that their password is never in your repository. One folder per client, always with the same structure.
objetivo: set up a client's folder with a fixed structure, human gates and secrets kept out of the repository, so you can deliver with agents without losing control.

aprende.t: The folder structure that repeats for every client
Where the agent works and where only a human decides
Why the gate is never skipped, even when you're in a hurry
Secrets outside the repository and the model through the subscription

hero_alt: Professional in front of two monitors with a terminal and an editor open, in a calm office.

nos.detalhe: docs, Search Console data, reports, briefings, scripts. The same for every client: the agent and you know where everything is. The secret stays in a .env that doesn't go to git.

Research, opportunity, briefing, draft, checklist, publishing, monitoring. The model runs through the subscription (Claude Code or Codex) whenever possible; paid API only with authorization for that specific purpose.
The client (or you, on their behalf) approves the list of pages and topics for the month. Nothing is written before that.
A human reviews each page: 10 to 20 minutes, with a summary of what changed and the things that need confirmation. Without approval, it doesn't publish.
Weekly export, inspection, report. What went up and what got stuck become the list for the next gate 1.

secoes.volta: Every month: monitoring feeds the next gate 1
secoes.legenda: The agent speeds up the work; the gates protect the client's trust.

secoes.titulo: How to set up the delivery

texto: Create the folder with the fixed structure and an instructions file for the agent (AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md) with the client's rules: tone, what not to publish, who approves.
Versioned in git: every change has a date and an author, and can be undone.
Keys and credentials live in environment variables, never in the repository or in the prompt.
Access to the client's dashboards is read-only, authorized in writing (lesson 7).
If the client doesn't have time to review, the cadence slows down. The gate is not skipped.
Help: the agent delivers the summary of what changed and the 3 things for the client to confirm.

exemplo.texto: A links script picked up the wrong course name in a subfolder. It was caught in the pilot, before the push. That's what running small and checking beforehand is for.

passos.sub: a number that doesn't add up
texto: Every number the agent produces goes through a cross-check: the part can't be bigger than the whole.
At INEMA, an export summed branded impressions by query and page and came out higher than the week's total. The fix was to sum by query only.

secoes.sub: Copy it and swap out what's between < >.

blocos.conteudo:
mkdir -p <cliente>/{docs,briefings,reports,scripts,data/gsc}
cd <cliente> && git init -b main
printf '.env\n*.key\ncredenciais/\n' > .gitignore
touch .env AGENTS.md data/urls-chave.txt data/consultas-alvo.txt

blocos.rot: Structure (template for the INEMA working repo)
blocos.conteudo:
docs/        diagnosis, plan, proposal, authorization
briefings/   <slug>.md, one per page
data/gsc/    weekly export (append-only)
reports/     semana-<data>.md, mensal-<mês>.md
scripts/     X-ray, export, report
AGENTS.md    client rules for the agent
.env         secret (kept out of git)

# Rules — <client>
- Tone: <how the client speaks>. Audience: <who>.
- Every number or quote comes from a client source; with no source, mark it PENDING and do not publish.
- Before publishing: complete quality checklist.
- Gate 1: <name> approves the month's list. Gate 2: <name> approves each page.
- Never: publish without approval, a big batch all at once, a page per keyword variation.
- Model through the subscription. Paid API only with written authorization for the purpose.
- Secrets only in .env. Never print a key in a log or report.

secoes.sub: It can be your own site as client zero.

exercicios.titulo: E1 · Folder with the secret kept out
exercicios.texto: Create the folder with the structure, the .gitignore and the filled-in AGENTS.md. Make the first commit.
exercicios.pronto: the git status command does not show the .env, the AGENTS.md has the tone, the source rule, both gates with a name and the API rule, and the first commit exists.

exercicios.texto: Write down who approves each gate, how long it takes, and what happens if that person has no time that week.
exercicios.pronto: the list has both gates with a name, time in minutes, and the sentence "if there is no review, the cadence drops; the gate is not skipped".

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: The client disappeared on vacation and didn't review the week's pages. What do you do?
opcoes: Publish, because the agent already reviewed them.
Hold the publication: the cadence drops, the gate is not skipped.
perguntas.explica: The gate is what gives the service its credibility. Skipping it once is what creates the problem you can't explain afterward.

perguntas.p: Where does the client's Search Console read credential live?
opcoes: In AGENTS.md, so the agent can find it.
In a .env kept out of git, loaded at run time.
perguntas.explica: A secret in the repository or in the prompt leaks through a commit, log or report. The .gitignore makes sure it doesn't get pushed.

perguntas.p: The agent says the week's branded impressions were higher than the total. What does that indicate?
opcoes: That the site grew a lot.
A sum error: the part can't be bigger than the whole. At INEMA, summing by query and page counted the same impression more than once.
That Google's dashboard got it wrong.
perguntas.explica: A simple cross-check calculation catches the agent's error before it goes into the client's report.

perguntas.p: Where can the agent work without human approval?
opcoes: Researching, drafting and building the report; publishing and choosing what to do go through the gates.
On everything, if it's a good agent.
perguntas.explica: The repetitive work is the agent's. Deciding what to do and what goes live is the human's.

itens.texto: Fixed structure, git, AGENTS.md with the client's rules.
What to do and what to publish. Without review, the cadence drops; the gate stays.
.env in .gitignore, model through the subscription, paid API only when authorized.
